summary: 49-year-old man with untreated hypertension: 2 days of severe headache, vomiting and blurred vision, now confused; BP 238/138, papilloedema, creatinine 188, proteinuria. ESC: ICU, IV labetalol/nicardipine, MAP down 20-25 % over hours.

inputs.hpi: Referred for a lipoma on the back. Two days of a severe generalised headache, vomiting and blurred vision; wife says he has become muddled today. Told he had high blood pressure 3 years ago but never started treatment.

exam.neuro: GCS 14 (E4 V4 M6), no focal deficit, no neck stiffness.
exam.other: Fundoscopy: bilateral papilloedema with flame haemorrhages and cotton-wool spots.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Hypertensive emergency - hypertensive encephalopathy / malignant hypertension
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Hypertensive emergency with encephalopathy, grade 4 retinopathy and AKI: emergency transfer to intensive care for IV labetalol or nicardipine, MAP reduction 20-25% over several hours.

mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: Web run 2026-09-25: not in top 3 of web.pane: 1. Inguinal / Femoral Hernia | 2. Acute Cholecystitis | 3. GORD / Reflux Oesophagitis; also in web.symptomInference#1, web.passive#1. PANE has no hypertensive-emergency node.
mustNotMiss.proposedFix: hypertensive_urgency prompt: classify as emergency when SBP >=180 (or DBP >=120) with acute organ damage words (confusion, encephalopathy, papilloedema, chest pain, pulmonary oedema, AKI, visual loss, pregnancy) regardless of the SBP >=220 cut-off; add triage emergency and ICU/IV labetalol-nicardipine; never offer oral amlodipine as the first action in an emergency.

mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: Web run 2026-09-25: not in top 3 of web.pane: 1. Inguinal / Femoral Hernia | 2. Acute Cholecystitis | 3. GORD / Reflux Oesophagitis; also in web.symptomInference#2, web.passive#2. PANE has no stroke or intracranial haemorrhage node.
mustNotMiss.proposedFix: PANE: add stroke/intracranial haemorrhage as must-not-miss nodes for headache + confusion.

mustInclude.note: Encephalopathy: brain imaging to exclude stroke/haemorrhage.
mustInclude.knownGapNote: Web run 2026-09-25: none of 22 investigation items matched (sources: web.clinicalPrompts, web.pane.seeded). First items: FBC, U&E (pre-operative bloods) (inguinal_hernia) | FBC, CRP (cholecystitis) | LFTs, bilirubin, ALP, GGT (cholecystitis) | Amylase / lipase (exclude pancreatitis) (cholecystitis).
mustInclude.proposedFix: Hypertension prompt: add CT head as an investigation when encephalopathy/confusion or focal signs are recorded.

mustInclude.note: IV labetalol or nicardipine in a monitored setting.

guideline.name: 2018 ESC/ESH Guidelines for the management of arterial hypertension
guideline.section: Section 8.3 hypertensive emergencies: severe hypertension with acute hypertension-mediated organ damage (encephalopathy, malignant hypertension, ACS, acute pulmonary oedema, aortic dissection, eclampsia) needs immediate, controlled BP reduction with IV therapy in a monitored setting (for hypertensive encephalopathy/malignant hypertension MAP reduction of 20-25% within several hours); severe hypertension without acute organ damage is not an emergency - oral therapy, no rapid reduction
guideline.citation: Williams B, Mancia G, Spiering W, et al. Eur Heart J. 2018;39:3021-3104.

guideline.name: ESC Council on Hypertension position document on the management of hypertensive emergencies
guideline.section: Hypertensive emergency: admission to intensive care, IV labetalol or nicardipine (clevidipine) first-line for encephalopathy/malignant hypertension; fundoscopy, ECG, creatinine, urinalysis, troponin; avoid precipitous falls
guideline.citation: van den Born BJH, Lip GYH, Brguljan-Hitij J, et al. Eur Heart J Cardiovasc Pharmacother. 2019;5:37-46.

rationale: Base hypertensive emergency: acute organ damage (encephalopathy, retinopathy, AKI) makes it an emergency. The web hypertension prompt keys on SBP (>=180 urgency, >=220 emergency actions); triage ignores BP.
